root_help:
nlm — Command-line interface to Google's NotebookLM.
Manage notebooks, sources, chat, and generated content from the terminal.

First run: `nlm auth` to set up authentication, or set NLM_AUTH_TOKEN and NLM_COOKIES.

Usage: nlm <command> [arguments]

Notebook Commands:
  notebook list [flags]                      List all notebooks
  notebook create <title>                    Create a new notebook
  notebook delete <notebook-id>              Delete a notebook
  notebook rename <notebook-id> <new-title>  Rename a notebook
  notebook emoji <notebook-id> <emoji>       Change notebook emoji
  notebook description <notebook-id> [text]  Set notebook description / creator notes (text via arg or stdin; empty clears)
  notebook cover <notebook-id> <preset-id>   Pick a built-in cover image (preset ID; HAR-captured value: 4. Other IDs uncatalogued)
  notebook cover-image <notebook-id> <image-path> Upload a custom cover image and associate it with the notebook
  notebook unrecent <notebook-id>            Remove a notebook from the recently-viewed list (does not delete it)
  notebook featured                          List featured notebooks
  analytics <notebook-id>                    Show notebook analytics time series

Source Commands:
  source list <notebook-id>                  List sources in notebook
  source add [flags] <notebook-id> <source...> Add one or more sources (files, URLs, or text; pass '-' to stream stdin as a single source)
  source sync [flags] <notebook-id> [path...] Bundle local files into a txtar source and keep it in sync (auto-chunks at 5MB; see --help)
  source pack [flags] [path...]              Preview the txtar bytes that sync would upload (offline)
  source delete <notebook-id> <source-id|-|a,b,c> Remove one or more sources (pass '-' to read newline-delimited IDs from stdin)
  source rename <source-id> <new-name>       Rename a source
  source refresh <notebook-id> <source-id>   Refresh source content
  source check <notebook-id> <source-id>     Check source freshness (Google-Drive-only; notebook-id enables client-side source-type validation)
  source read [--format text|markdown|html|json|raw] <notebook-id> <source-id> Read a source body
  discover-sources <notebook-id> <query>     Discover relevant sources via Es3dTe (chat fallback if the server rejects)

Note Commands:
  note list <notebook-id>                    List notes in notebook
  note read [--format text|markdown|html] [--out file] [--open] <notebook-id> <note-id> Read full note content
  note create <notebook-id> <title> [--content TEXT | --content-file FILE] Create new note (content via arg or stdin)
  note update <notebook-id> <note-id> [--title TITLE] [--content TEXT | --content-file FILE] Edit note content and title
  note delete <notebook-id> <note-id>        Remove a note from a notebook

Label Commands:
  label list <notebook-id>                   List labels (autolabel clusters) in a notebook
  label generate <notebook-id>               Recompute autolabel clusters for a notebook
  label create <notebook-id> <name> [emoji]  Create a new manual label on a notebook
  label rename <notebook-id> <label-id> <new-name> Rename an existing label
  label emoji <notebook-id> <label-id> <emoji> Set or clear the emoji on a label
  label delete <notebook-id> <label-id> [<label-id>...] Delete one or more labels by ID
  label unlabeled <notebook-id>              Apply existing labels to currently-unlabeled sources
  label relabel-all <notebook-id>            Re-cluster everything (UI's "Relabel all")
  label attach <notebook-id> <label-id|name> <source-id|name> Attach a source to a label (single source per call)

Create Commands:
  app create [flags] <notebook-id> <instructions...> Create a generated app artifact
  mindmap create [flags] <notebook-id> <instructions...> Create a generated mind map artifact
  create-audio [flags] <notebook-id> <instructions...> Create audio overview
  create-video [flags] <notebook-id> <instructions...> Create video overview
  app-create [flags] <notebook-id> <instructions...> Create a generated app artifact
  mindmap-create [flags] <notebook-id> <instructions...> Create a generated mind map artifact
  create-slides [flags] <notebook-id> [instructions...] Create slide deck
  create-report [flags] <notebook-id> <report-type> [description...] Create a report artifact (run report-suggestions for valid types)

Audio Commands:
  audio list <notebook-id>                   List audio overviews for a notebook
  audio create [flags] <notebook-id> <instructions...> Create audio overview
  audio get <notebook-id>                    Get audio overview details
  audio download <notebook-id> [filename]    Download audio file
  audio delete <notebook-id>                 Delete audio overview
  audio share <notebook-id>                  Share audio overview

Video Commands:
  video create [flags] <notebook-id> <instructions...> Create video overview

Deck Commands:
  deck create [flags] <notebook-id> [instructions...] Create slide deck
  deck download [flags] <notebook-id>        Download a slide deck (PDF/PPTX)

Artifact Commands:
  artifact list <notebook-id>                List artifacts in notebook
  artifact get <artifact-id>                 Get artifact details
  artifact read <artifact-id>                Print a text artifact
  artifact export [flags] <artifact-id>      Export an artifact
  artifact update [--name <name>] <artifact-id> [title] Rename artifact (new title from positional arg or --name)
  artifact delete <artifact-id>              Delete artifact
  read-artifact <artifact-id>                Print a text artifact

Guidebook Commands:
  guidebooks                                 List all guidebooks
  guidebook <guidebook-id>                   Get guidebook details
  guidebook-details <guidebook-id>           Get detailed guidebook info with sections and analytics
  guidebook-publish <guidebook-id>           Publish a guidebook
  guidebook-share <guidebook-id>             Share a guidebook
  guidebook-ask <guidebook-id> <question>    Ask a guidebook question
  guidebook-rm <guidebook-id>                Delete a guidebook

Generation Commands:
  generate-guide <notebook-id>               Generate notebook guide
  source-guide [flags] <notebook-id> [source-id...] Show the per-source auto-summary and keyword chips (cached on disk)
  generate-chat [flags] <notebook-id> [prompt...] Stream a one-shot chat answer (use --conversation to follow up)
  report-suggestions <notebook-id>           Suggest report topics for notebook
  audio-suggestions <notebook-id>            Suggest audio-overview blueprints (emit JSON lines; pipe to create-audio)
  generate-report [flags] <notebook-id>      Generate multi-section report via chat (see --prompt, --sections)

Chat Commands:
  chat list [notebook-id]                    List chat sessions (server-side when a notebook is given)
  chat history <notebook-id> <conversation-id> View conversation history
  chat show [flags] <notebook-id> [conversation-id] Render a local chat transcript (see --citations)
  chat delete <notebook-id>                  Delete server-side chat history
  chat config <notebook-id> goal default | <notebook-id> goal custom <prompt...> | <notebook-id> length <default|longer|shorter> Configure chat settings
  chat instructions set <notebook-id> "prompt" Set system instructions
  chat instructions get <notebook-id>        Show current system instructions
  chat [flags] <notebook-id> [conversation-id | prompt...] Open interactive chat (one-shot if a prompt is given; -f <file> reads a long prompt from file)

Research Commands:
  research [flags] <notebook-id> <query...>  Run fast or deep research (JSON-lines by default; --md for markdown; --mode=fast|deep)

Sharing Commands:
  share <notebook-id>                        Share notebook publicly
  share-private <notebook-id>                Share notebook privately
  share-details <share-id>                   Get details of shared project

Other Commands:
  mcp                                        Run the MCP server on stdin/stdout
  auth [login] [options] [profile-name]      Set up authentication from a browser profile
  refresh                                    Refresh stored authentication credentials
  account [set <key> <value>]                Show or update the authenticated user's NotebookLM account (ZwVcOc / hT54vc)

Exit Codes:
  0  success
  2  bad arguments
  3  authentication required or invalid
  4  not found (notebook, source, artifact)
  5  precondition failed (quota, source cap, wrong source type)
  6  transient error (rate limit, 5xx, connection)
  7  resource busy (still generating)

commands.name: source add
commands.summary: Add one or more sources (files, URLs, or text; pass '-' to stream stdin as a single source)
commands.help:
Usage: nlm source add [flags] <notebook-id> <source...>

Sources may be files, URLs, or text literals. A sole '-' streams all of
stdin in as a single source (pair with --name and --mime-type). To add a
list of sources from stdin, compose with xargs.

Flags:
  --name, -n <name>         Custom name for the added source
  --mime, --mime-type <t>   Override MIME detection for file/stdin content
  --replace <source-id>     Upload a replacement, then delete the old source
  --pre-process <cmd>       Pipe each non-URL source through 'sh -c cmd' before
                            upload; stdout replaces the content. Non-zero exit
                            aborts the batch. URL sources are passed through.
  --chunk <bytes>           Split each non-URL source into parts of at most <bytes>
                            each. Parts upload as "name", "name (pt2)", ... Use for
                            content that exceeds the per-request size limit without
                            switching to `nlm sync` txtar bundling.

Examples:
  nlm source add <notebook-id> https://example.com/article
  nlm source add --name "API notes" <notebook-id> ./notes.txt
  cat notes.md | nlm source add --name "April notes" <notebook-id> -
  cat urls.txt | xargs nlm source add <notebook-id>
  nlm source add --pre-process 'pandoc -f docx -t markdown' <notebook-id> brief.docx
  nlm source add --chunk 5242880 <notebook-id> huge.log

commands.name: source sync
commands.summary: Bundle local files into a txtar source and keep it in sync (auto-chunks at 5MB; see --help)
commands.help:
Usage: nlm source sync [flags] <notebook-id> [path...]

(also available as the top-level shortcut: nlm sync)

Bundles local files into a txtar archive and uploads them as a single named
source. Re-running sync updates that source in place: unchanged content is
skipped via a hash cache, and archives larger than --max-bytes are split into
numbered parts ("name", "name (pt2)", ...).

Path handling:
  (no paths)                Sync the current directory
  <dir>                     Include files tracked by git ls-files (falls back
                            to a recursive walk; skips .git, node_modules,
                            __pycache__, .eggs)
  <file>                    Include that file verbatim
  -                         Read newline-delimited paths from stdin

Binary files are detected and skipped. Text files containing lines that look
like txtar markers are safely quoted so the archive round-trips.

Flags:
  --name, -n <name>         Source title (defaults to the basename of the
                            single path; required with multiple paths or stdin)
  --force                   Re-upload even when the content hash is unchanged
  --dry-run                 Print the plan (add/update/skip/delete) without
                            contacting the server
  --max-bytes <n>           Per-chunk size threshold (default 5120000)
  --json                    Emit NDJSON progress records instead of text
  --exclude <pattern>       Skip files matching a filepath.Match pattern;
                            tested against the full path and basename. May
                            be repeated. Trailing '/' or '/'-bearing patterns
                            match as path prefixes (e.g. 'vendor/'). A
                            .nlmignore file at the repo root adds patterns
                            automatically (one per line, '#' comments).
  --include-untracked       Include untracked, non-ignored files when syncing
                            git directories

Usage: nlm source pack [flags] [path...]

(also available as the top-level shortcut: nlm sync-pack)

archive to stdout without contacting the server. Useful for previewing what
sync would upload, or for piping into tools that consume txtar.

when the bundle would be split. Pass --chunk N to emit the Nth chunk.

  --chunk <n>               Emit the Nth chunk (1-indexed) when multiple
  --exclude <pattern>       Skip files matching the pattern (repeatable;
                            same rules as sync)
  --pre-process <cmd>       Pipe each discovered file through 'sh -c cmd' before
                            bundling (same semantics as sync)

commands.name: sync
commands.summary: Bundle local files into a txtar source and keep it in sync (auto-chunks at 5MB; see --help)
commands.help:
Usage: nlm sync [flags] <notebook-id> [path...]

Bundles local files into a txtar archive and uploads them as a single named
source. Re-running sync updates that source in place: unchanged content is
skipped via a hash cache, and archives larger than --max-bytes are split into
numbered parts ("name", "name (pt2)", ...).

Path handling:
  (no paths)                Sync the current directory
  <dir>                     Include files tracked by git ls-files (falls back
                            to a recursive walk; skips .git, node_modules,
                            __pycache__, .eggs)
  <file>                    Include that file verbatim
  -                         Read newline-delimited paths from stdin

Binary files are detected and skipped. Text files containing lines that look
like txtar markers are safely quoted so the archive round-trips.

Flags:
  --name, -n <name>         Source title (defaults to the basename of the
                            single path; required with multiple paths or stdin)
  --force                   Re-upload even when the content hash is unchanged
  --dry-run                 Print the plan (add/update/skip/delete) without
                            contacting the server
  --max-bytes <n>           Per-chunk size threshold (default 5120000)
  --json                    Emit NDJSON progress records instead of text
  --exclude <pattern>       Skip files matching a filepath.Match pattern;
                            tested against the full path and basename. May
                            be repeated. Trailing '/' or '/'-bearing patterns
                            match as path prefixes (e.g. 'vendor/'). A
                            .nlmignore file at the repo root adds patterns
                            automatically (one per line, '#' comments).
  --include-untracked       Include untracked, non-ignored files when syncing
                            git directories
  --parallel <n>            Max concurrent chunk uploads (default 4; use a
                            negative value to force serial)
  --pre-process <cmd>       Pipe each discovered file through 'sh -c cmd' before
                            bundling; stdout replaces the bundled bytes (and
                            participates in the hash). $NLM_FILE_NAME holds the
                            file name. Non-zero exit aborts the sync.

Hash cache: ~/.cache/nlm/sync/<notebook-id>/

Examples:
  nlm sync <notebook-id>                    # sync the current directory
  nlm sync -n docs <notebook-id> ./docs ./notes
  nlm sync --dry-run <notebook-id>          # preview without uploading
  nlm sync --force <notebook-id> README.md  # force re-upload
  nlm sync --exclude '*.pb.go' --exclude 'vendor/' <notebook-id>
  git ls-files '*.go' | nlm sync -n go-src <notebook-id> -
  nlm sync --pre-process 'jq .' <notebook-id> ./logs   # reformat JSON before bundling

commands.name: sync-pack
commands.summary: Preview the txtar bytes that sync would upload (offline)
commands.help:
Usage: nlm sync-pack [flags] [path...]

Runs the same discover/bundle pipeline as sync but writes the resulting txtar
archive to stdout without contacting the server. Useful for previewing what
sync would upload, or for piping into tools that consume txtar.

With no --chunk flag: emits the sole chunk, or lists chunk sizes to stderr
when the bundle would be split. Pass --chunk N to emit the Nth chunk.

Flags:
  --name, -n <name>         Source title (same rules as sync)
  --max-bytes <n>           Per-chunk size threshold (default 5120000)
  --chunk <n>               Emit the Nth chunk (1-indexed) when multiple
  --exclude <pattern>       Skip files matching the pattern (repeatable;
                            same rules as sync)
  --pre-process <cmd>       Pipe each discovered file through 'sh -c cmd' before
                            bundling (same semantics as sync)

Examples:
  nlm sync-pack                                  # pack the current directory
  nlm sync-pack ./docs > docs.txtar
  nlm sync-pack --chunk 2 ./docs
  nlm sync-pack --exclude '*.pb.go' ./src

commands.name: betool
commands.summary: Translate raw batchexecute payloads to JSON and back (offline codec)
commands.help:
usage: nlm betool <mode> [flags] [file...]

Translate raw batchexecute network payloads to a readable summary or JSON, and
back. Reads from [file], or from stdin when [file] is "-" or omitted. Performs
no network I/O.

Modes:
  decode-request    raw "f.req=...&at=...&" body      -> text (--json for JSON)
  encode-request    JSON request spec                 -> raw form body
  decode-response   raw ")]}'"-prefixed response body -> text (--json for JSON)
  encode-response   JSON response spec                -> raw response body
  infer-proto       raw response payloads             -> descriptor textproto
  audit-corpus      JSONL traffic files               -> per-RPC verification
  augment-corpus    descriptor set and JSONL traffic  -> augmented descriptor set

infer-proto flags:
  --rpc-id=<id>     select the response descriptor; required for inference
  --samples=<dir>   infer from every regular file in a directory
                    (multiple input files may also be listed; raw responses,
                    HAR, JSONL traffic, and httprr recordings are accepted)
  --descriptor=<f>  augment a binary FileDescriptorSet instead of the built-in schema
  --message=<name>  fully-qualified root message in --descriptor; required with it
  --output=<f>      write the augmented binary FileDescriptorSet to a file
  --json            emit the descriptor as protojson instead of focused proto text

augment-corpus flags:
  --descriptor=<f>  binary FileDescriptorSet to augment
  --rpc-option=<n>  string MethodOptions extension containing captured RPC IDs
  --boolean-option=<n>
                    bool FieldOptions extension marking JSON boolean encoding
  --min-observations=<n>
                    require n consistent observations before mutation (default 2)
  --output=<f>      write the augmented binary FileDescriptorSet
  --json            emit the evidence and mutation report as JSON

Decode modes print a human-readable summary by default; pass the global --json
flag (before the mode: "nlm --json betool decode-response …") for the full
structured output. The encode modes consume that JSON, so round-tripping a
payload needs --json on the decode side.

Flags (decode modes only):
  --proto           decode into the proto message type bound to the rpc_id,
                    showing proto JSON with named fields
  --rpc-id=<id>     supply or override the rpc_id, or a method name to
                    disambiguate a shared rpc_id (e.g. CreateVideoOverview)
  --verify          (implies --proto) re-encode the proto back to wire and
                    report whether the round-trip is lossless, plus the wire
                    positions the proto type does not model, grouped by
                    normalized path (with --json: "roundtrip_lossless",
                    "missing_field_count", "missing_field_groups")
  --verify-all      (implies --verify) also attach the full unabridged list of
                    findings ("missing_fields")
	  --infer-missing   (alias: --infer; implies --verify) show inferred missing fields as a
                    compact source-style proto fragment

Examples:
  # Inspect a request captured from a HAR:
  pbpaste | nlm betool decode-request

  # Decode a response into its typed proto message:
  nlm betool decode-response --proto resp.txt

  # A response body has no rpc_id, so supply it:
  nlm betool decode-response --proto --rpc-id=CCqFvf resp.txt

  # Round-trip a response body (encode consumes JSON, so decode with --json):
  nlm --json betool decode-response resp.txt | nlm betool encode-response

  # Hand-craft a request body from JSON:
  echo '{"rpcs":[{"id":"wXbhsf","args":[]}],"at":"TOKEN"}' \
    | nlm betool encode-request

  # Audit every RPC request and response in captured JSONL traffic:
  nlm --json betool audit-corpus "$NLM_CORPUS_DIR"/*/notebooklm.google.com/*.jsonl

  # Add evidence-backed fields to an external descriptor set:
  nlm --json betool augment-corpus --descriptor=input.pb \
    --rpc-option=example.rpc_id --output=augmented.pb traffic.jsonl
